title: Chole Bhature
description: A Delhi street-food classic of spicy chickpea curry (chole) served with large, fluffy deep-fried bread (bhature). Often accompanied by pickled onions, green chillies and a glass of lassi.
ingredients: Chickpeas, tea leaves or amchur for colour and tang
Onion, tomato, ginger-garlic, chole masala, garam masala
steps: Soak and cook chickpeas with tea or spices until soft.
Prepare a spicy onion-tomato gravy and simmer the chickpeas in it.
Knead a soft dough for bhature, rest, roll and deep-fry until puffed and golden.
Serve hot chole with bhature, onion and pickle.
tips: The best versions have soft, airy bhature and deeply flavoured, slightly sour chole.

title: Stuffed Paratha (Paranthe Wali Gali style)
description: Crispy, ghee-fried stuffed flatbreads from the legendary Paranthe Wali Gali in Chandni Chowk. Classic fillings include aloo, gobhi, paneer, dal or mixed vegetables, served with pickle, chutney and curd.
ingredients: Potato / cauliflower / paneer filling with spices
steps: Prepare a soft dough and a well-spiced stuffing.
Stuff, seal and roll into parathas.
Shallow-fry on a tawa with generous ghee until golden and crisp on both sides.
Serve hot with pickle and yogurt.
tips: Traditional shops in Paranthe Wali Gali have been serving these since the 19th century.

title: Nihari with Khameeri Roti
description: Slow-cooked overnight mutton (or beef) stew enriched with marrow, spices and a wheat-flour thickening. Traditionally eaten for breakfast with soft khameeri roti. A classic Mughlai dish of Old Delhi.
ingredients: Ginger, garlic, whole spices, wheat flour for thickening
steps: Slow-cook the meat overnight or for many hours with spices until extremely tender.
Thicken the gravy with a wheat-flour slurry if needed.
Finish with fried onions and ginger.
Serve with khameeri or naan-style bread.
tips: The name comes from the Arabic ‘nahar’ (morning); it was traditionally a morning meal for labourers and soldiers.

title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
description: Delhi’s most famous culinary export — tandoori chicken simmered in a silky tomato-butter-cream gravy. Invented at Moti Mahal in the 1950s and now a global icon of Indian cuisine.
ingredients: Tomato puree, butter, cream, kasuri methi
Ginger, garlic, mild spices, sugar or honey for balance
steps: Prepare or use leftover tandoori chicken.
Cook a smooth tomato-based gravy with butter and spices.
Add chicken and simmer gently; finish with cream and kasuri methi.
Serve with naan or rice.
tips: Authentic Delhi versions are mildly spiced and rely on the smokiness of the tandoori chicken.

title: Dal Makhani
description: Slow-cooked black lentils (urad) and kidney beans finished with butter and cream. A rich Punjabi dish that became a Delhi restaurant classic and is now inseparable from the city’s North Indian repertoire.
steps: Soak and slow-cook the dals until very soft (often overnight).
Prepare a tomato-butter base and combine with the dals.
Simmer on low heat for a long time, finishing with cream and kasuri methi.
Serve with naan or rice.
tips: The longer it cooks, the better the flavour and texture.

title: Seekh Kebab
description: Minced meat mixed with spices, moulded onto skewers and grilled over charcoal. A Mughlai staple of Old Delhi, often served with mint chutney, onion and roomali roti.
ingredients: Ginger, garlic, green chilli, garam masala, coriander
Fat for binding, oil for grilling
steps: Mix minced meat thoroughly with spices and bind well.
Shape onto skewers.
Grill over charcoal until cooked and lightly charred.
Serve hot with chutney and onion rings.
tips: The smoky charcoal flavour is essential to authentic Old Delhi kebabs.

title: Mutton Korma
description: Rich, aromatic Mughlai-style mutton cooked in a yogurt and fried-onion gravy with whole spices. A classic of Old Delhi restaurants such as Karim’s.
steps: Marinate mutton in yogurt and spices.
Cook with fried onions and whole spices on low heat until tender and the gravy is rich.
Finish with a touch of cream or more ghee if desired.
Serve with naan or sheermal.
tips: Patience and low heat yield the best results.

title: Paneer Butter Masala
description: Soft paneer cubes in a creamy tomato-butter gravy, the vegetarian counterpart to butter chicken. Extremely popular across Delhi restaurants and homes.
ingredients: Tomato puree, butter, cream, kasuri methi
steps: Prepare a smooth tomato-butter gravy.
Add paneer and simmer gently.
Finish with cream and kasuri methi.
Serve with naan or rice.
tips: Do not overcook the paneer or it becomes rubbery.

title: Aloo Tikki Chaat
description: Crispy potato patties topped with yogurt, tamarind and mint chutneys, chopped onion, sev and chaat masala. One of Delhi’s most beloved street-food chaat preparations.
steps: Mash potatoes with spices, shape into patties and shallow-fry until crisp.
Place on a plate, top with yogurt and both chutneys.
Garnish with onion, sev and chaat masala.
Serve immediately.
tips: The contrast of hot crispy tikki and cool yogurt is key.

title: Gol Gappe (Pani Puri)
description: Crisp hollow puris filled with spicy, tangy flavoured water (pani), mashed potato or chickpeas, and chutneys. Delhi’s favourite interactive street snack, also known as pani puri.
ingredients: Spicy mint-coriander pani, sweet tamarind pani
Boiled potato or chickpeas, chaat masala
steps: Prepare the flavoured waters and potato filling.
Crack a small hole in each puri, fill with potato and dunk into the pani.
Eat in one bite.
Repeat.
tips: The pani should be ice-cold and perfectly balanced between spicy and tangy.

title: Samosa
description: Crispy triangular pastry filled with spiced potato and peas, deep-fried until golden. A ubiquitous Delhi tea-time and street snack, often served with green and tamarind chutneys.
ingredients: Boiled potato, peas, cumin, coriander, chilli, garam masala
steps: Prepare a stiff dough and a spiced potato filling.
Shape into cones or triangles, fill and seal.
Deep-fry until crisp and golden.
Serve with chutneys.
tips: The pastry should be crisp; the filling well-spiced but not watery.

title: Jalebi
description: Crisp, syrup-soaked spiral sweets made from fermented batter and deep-fried. A classic Old Delhi sweet, often eaten with rabri or simply hot from the kadhai.
ingredients: Maida, yogurt or fermented starter, water
Sugar syrup flavoured with cardamom or saffron
steps: Prepare a fermented batter of the right consistency.
Pipe spirals into hot oil and fry until crisp and golden.
Immediately soak in warm sugar syrup.
Serve hot or warm.
tips: Best eaten fresh; they lose crispness if left too long.

title: Dahi Bhalla
description: Soft lentil dumplings (bhalla) soaked in creamy yogurt, topped with sweet and spicy chutneys, sev and chaat masala. A refined and popular chaat of Old Delhi.
ingredients: Thick yogurt, tamarind chutney, green chutney
steps: Soak, grind and deep-fry soft urad dal dumplings.
Soak them in water, then in seasoned yogurt.
Top with chutneys, sev and chaat masala.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
tips: The bhalla should be soft and absorbent.
